text_fidelity_a:
POC, Ventral Air MIPS Road Cycling Helmet with Performance Cooling We recently got an electric scooter, plus my wife rides roller blades, and we’re talking about an electric bike - or recumbent, not sure which. We have a need for a couple bike helmets. I will fully admit, we are NOT experts in this area and have done no research beyond knowing they need to be rated and that there are good ones and bad. We have each owned in the past - that kind that looks similar to this, but with that point at the back, which always makes us think, what happens if you land on the back and that point slams the helmet forward...

So when I had the chance to grab this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) I took it without hesitation. Not only does it look good, but in wearing it, it feels great and gives us a sense of being safer than without a helmet. And for all the helmets we have owned, that this has the blunted back, answers that “what if,”

So this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) arrived and we broke in right away - had to see it in person. We were blown away by the presentation - it comes in a nice box - make sure to take care of this box, it is your storage box! Inside you’ll find the helmet and a bag. Open up and the helmet goes in the bag in the box - it is a GREAT way to store your helmet! Our previous helmets always end up on a shelf somewhere. This is excellent and we were already impressed.

Next... the helmet. It looks cool. Not only the color - I’m a blue guy and it’s perfect - but the overall design is so cool. We both liked the matted look - over the glossy really - but in person it looks even better. And on, it looks seriously cool. I tried it with both my reading glasses - no point other than to see how well it handles glasses - and my sunglasses - one of several I own, so one design style - and in both cases they fit perfectly under the sides of the helmet. I felt like I could wear them for an hour and have no rub or discomfort. I have not actually worn them out riding yet, but in this situation, the test was impressive.

As to that idea we always wondered about - what happens if you land on the back and that point - this is blunted, meaning there is no point. You land and it makes sense - you’ll have the back side make contact, but in a way that appears it’ll cushion the head and not shove it or the helmet forward.

The helmet is really light weight and you cannot believe how it feels like it could be that light and protect your head. So we put it on... and for me it fit perfectly. I got the large due to my large head. I had to open the strap slightly, but one half turn on the wheel and it was perfect - snug, but not tight nor uncomfortable. Now we only have this one, so when my wife went out to test the scooter, she had to wear this one. She has a much smaller head than mine, but it was nothing to size this down for her - while she technically doesn’t fit their size chart at this size, it worked well - she was comfortable and felt completely secure in it. It was very easy to size down for her, then bring it back up for me. It was easy and quick and we both felt great with it on.

I’ll be honest - this price point is above what we would normally spend. I was able to get it as a Vine Reviewer and for that I am grateful. I normally do not speak to price because of that, but in this case, wish to address it. In talking about it, we WOULD spend the money to get a second one for her. We feel that the safety this “promises” is worth the money. Now that said, We would do much more research first - we are not experts on the safety aspects of helmets and would make sure first. There is NO way we would go out and test this - meaning risk our head to see that is does what it promises. But if our further research shows what we think it would, yes, we would consider spending the money. Brain safety is important and we want something good. Now that said, if there is a product at a lower price that provides equal safety, we would seriously consider that - money is something we are careful with, but so too our safety. In the end, this is an excellent helmet that fits well and comfortably. Safety is the priority. But we do have to be realistic about cost. So if we could afford it and our research indicates it is a value, then yes, we would pay, but if not, if we found something as good at a lower price point, we’d have to look in that direction.

But we both love this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) helmet and are thrilled to have it.
text_fidelity_b: POC, Ventral Air MIPS Road Cycling Helmet with Performance Cooling

text_fidelity_a:
Walker's Razor Slim The things I was curious about before buying these:
A) How they sound.
B) How they feel.
C) Compared to Howard Leights by Honeywell as well as the BT edition of the Walker Razor.

I have not tested the Noise Cancellation yet but provided it works as it should I wanted to get out my review in case anyone wondered what I did. My hand's on impressions have been fully positive.
If you get these and wonder how to open the package: I just bent the package in half. This caused the cardboard to split open and the plastic clamshell is not sealed - it is 2 parts and the headphones came out super simple.

How do they sound? (I own Sennheiser HD600 compared to those:)
A)Surprisingly good. Not audiophile but not bad.
B)Bass is light. Not much bass from these. Bass seems purposely reserved, truth be told probably neutral.
C)Slight emphasis on mid-range. But not annoying in any frequency.
D)Highs are present but not pristine.
E)Overall, they sound good for a $43 set of headphones that do so much more. I am pleased with it. I can listen without irritation.

How do they feel?
A) A little tight on my medium-sized head but the muffs are plushy and do a good job of distributing the clamp pressure.
B) I can't imagine wearing these for much more than an hour at a time but it might be ok for longer but probably no one will actually want to.
C) Headband doesn't rub my scalp.
D) No hair pulling or "pinchy parts".
E) The hinges that hold the muffs look thin but they work (so far). Durability could be a concern.
F) The hinges are adjustable. I collapsed then down about 2/5ths of the way so they could possibly fit larger heads but wider heads may have more clamp pressure?
G) Again, the clamp pressure is pretty tight. I am surprised how tight they are. But they stay on the head when moving my head which is good. It is a good thing they are tight but it could cause them to fatigue your head after a while. Be aware they are pretty tight on the head but I don't believe it will be a deal-breaker.

How is the enhanced hearing:
A) Fairly natural. I can rather accurately distinguish sounds.
B) I never knew what a bee flying sounded like other than Bumblebees right in my ear. I heard the bee and I will learn that sound but I wouldn't have known what it was had I not seen the bee and heard the sound.
C) You will discover new sounds you haven't heard before.
D) Unfortunately, the sound is mono-sounding like everyone has said. Determining the origin or placement of noises does not work out so well.
E) I questioned whether to get these or the Howard Leight by Honeywell. I decided to try these first after listening to YouTube videos. I have read reviews that say the "Howard's" better determine which direction noises come from but some videos said they do not do it better enough to choose them over these.
F) These are supposedly more comfortable than the Howard Leights.
G) They are cheaper and look better IMO than the Howard Leights.
H) I might buy the Howard Leights just to see if the sound placement is better because I think that would be a big deal but from what I have read and heard the hype may or may not be all it is cracked up to be. The reviewers mostly chose these over the Howard Leight.

Overall, I am impressed that these are only $43.
Be sure to get a 3.5mm to 3.5mm male to male wire to use them for music.
I wanted to get the Bluetooth version but after reading how much problems people were having with the BT dropping or not working, I decided to get the wired version.
The BT version has 4 mics which, on paper, seems would give better awareness of surroundings but from things I heard it didn't quite work as well in RL as it seems it would. I still would like to try those because it would be worth the money to me if they worked like they should but if they didn't I knew I would still be getting these.
text_fidelity_b: Walker's Razor Slim

Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency Purchased this Lighting Ever 1000 lumens lantern and the Rayovac Sportsman 240 Lumen LED Lantern SE3DLNACOM on the same order. Not realizing the identical nature of each lantern at the time, having both in hand together allowed me to make a side by side comparison. This might help someone chose which one to buy.

The Rayovac I purchased on this page shows a 240 lumen lantern, however the one that arrived clearly states 305 lumens. Physically, the LE and RV are manufactured almost identically in composition. Both require 3 D sized batteries to operate. The LE is only one ounce more than the RV, but the LE feels and looks sturdier and of higher quality. LE and RV will be used when describing each lantern, but keep in mind that I am comparing the Rayovac 305 lumen that arrived, versus what is advertised on the Amazon page.

The LE's output on highest mode is 1000 lumens compared to the RV's highest mode at 305; both are daylight white on high. On high, the LE touts a run time of 18 hours (10 watts), to the RV's 70 hours (4 watts), RV wins on run time.

The LE's second mode both reduces the lumens (dimmer) and changes the color temp to a warm white. While the RV does not have a color temp variable, it does provide an option to dim the output to 140 lumens for its 2nd mode and can run 140 hours. LE wins due to the option to change to preferred temperature color.

The LE's 18 hour operation will increase to 25 hours when on mode 2 (warm white). The third mode of the LE further dims the light and combines the warm and daylight temperatures to somewhere in between. The paperwork for the LE shows that mode 3 will last only 12 hours, which does not make sense as to why it shortens the life by the most .

The last mode for both (LE's 4th mode, RVs 3rd mode) is a blinking / strobe light of the daylight / cool white color. I've not much to say on this mode - does not seem relevant at the moment to me. The RV has one final feature though, which is a dim green light on the power button that blinks very slowly, to assist the owner in locating it during periods of darkness. Personally, I do not like this feature and would either remove the batteries or put a dimmit over the light. Buyers might prefer this, I'm just not a fan of idiot lights with or without power.

Lastly, I mentioned these being cut from the same mold, and both have battery compartments in the base of the lantern. The LE has a stem mounted in the base that the cover's slot must align correctly to close the battery compartment. The RV has a slot (no stem) on the rim of base to align to the cover's slot opening. However, the LE cover is still much easier to close with the batteries in the unit. Once the appropriate alignment is met, you must push down and turn to close the base. Think of pushing a child-proof pill bottle's lid to open it. Do the same on these lanterns. The LE base closed after 3 tries, to the RV's numerous tries getting frustrated. LE wins on battery replacement procedures.

Overall, the LE wins hands down. For a 15 ounce lantern with more features, I paid approximately 17.00. The 14 ounce RV cost $24, but the Amazon page shows the list price at $34 and the buyer was getting a $10 discount at purchase. Though the 4 watt RV runs much longer at 2.9 days or 5.8 on mode 2 and the 10 watt LE has a run time of .75 days or 1 full day on mode 2, I am not using this to go camping. This was purchased for power failures, to be used as part of an overall emergency preparedness plan, and bright is what we need indoors during power failures. The hours will be broken up over various times and 18 hours will get us several days. For the money, same battery requirements and functionality, LE takes the cake.

I've never heard of Lighting Ever before, but the product packaging shows they have their home base in Las Vegas, NV, another in the UK and one in China, where this lamp was made. It comes with RoHS certification, 1 year warranty and the instructions are the most accurate regarding the English language than I've seen in a long time. How refreshing to receive grammatically correct documents included in the box (yes, a real box). The RayOVac has a limited lifetime warranty and came in a plastic transparent bag, unbranded. The TLC shows on the LE, while the product packing on the RV is a wrapped label with specs, and it is though product presentation was an afterthought. For the $24, some type of protection during delivery wouldn't hurt. Whoever LE is, I will buy again if they produce a product as good as this one.
text_fidelity_b: Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency

First of all, the price is on point and provides a huge savings over having to buy each of the items included individually. Second, we love the watertight hardback case that the tools come in. It has strong clasps on three sides and they don't just pop open. You have to tug pretty hard on them, so that actually is important so you don't lose your gear when you're on the move and may need it most. Second, the tactical gear that is included isn't cheaply made. These are durable products, such as the tactical pen (with a glass breaker on one end), flashlight (needs one AA battery), and the knife. Even the compass is fairly weighty in your hand and works very well. Also, because of the amount of detail that goes into these items, this whole kit makes a handsome gift that any outdoorsman would appreciate too. We also like the tactical bracelet because even if that is all you have on you, there is also a flint built in so you can start a fire, a whistle, and a compass. Also, it is made of paracord, so you can use it to tie up an emergency shelter or go fishing if need be. The manual that comes with it is detailed, but you will want to become well familiar with each item included and how to use it before you head out to the woods or on your trek as you may try to outrun a storm. Also, there are a few items included such as the glass breaker end of the pen, the saw, and of course the knife, which could cut someone, particularly a child, so you'll want to make sure those who handle it aren't going to accidentally injure themselves because these items are definitely not toys. This hoola hoop is definitely very sturdy and well made.

It comes in several pieces that link together so you can adjust it to fit your waist and ideally remove pieces as you lose weight. The pieces link together very well, it feels very secure. The weight is also very secure in the hoola hoop.

I find it to be a really fun way to work out. You do feel the burn with this especially if you do the full recommended 30 mins. It took me 2 days to get the hang of it, I watched a couple youtube videos for some tips. Basically, you want to shift your weight side to side rather than do a full circular motion with your hips.

I have been using it for about 2 weeks now - about every other day and I noticed a slight decrease in my waist but nothing crazy yet, though I do believe doing this for a month at least 5 days a week will give you noticeable results.

Currently, I am able to go for about 10 mins straight without stopping at all. Whenever I stop, I switch directions. The only downside that I have noticed is when I use it in the opposite direction, the counter on the hoop doesn't count those spins. It only counts going in one direction. I don't know if that's just something wrong with my counter or if that's how it's made but ultimately it's not that big of an issue (though it would be nice to have an accurate count of my total spins at the end of the workout).

Also, it is loud like others have mentioned - but I think all of these kind of hoola hoops are. If you wear headphones you can easily listen to a podcast or watch youtube or something - but you can't really without headphones.

Overall, if you're looking for a weighted hoola hoop, this one is a good one!

Ringside Gel Boxing MMA Hand Wraps Once in a while a product comes along that looks like it might pose a solution to a different problem than what it is actually intended for. These Ringside Gel Wraps are obviously designed to protect your hands while either working out or sparring in the ring. But I ordered them for a different unrelated purpose -- protecting my knuckles while cutting/trimming trees in our wetlands. We live in Southwest Florida where the brush grows all year around and not only grows quickly but also tries to choke out its neighbors by fighting for the available sunlight and water. That makes for tight quarters and a lot of "barked" knuckles while maneuvering tools and changing positions.

There are pros and cons to how this product is constructed:

PROS
1. They fit your hands ergonomically without limiting your flexibility. I am actually typing this review with the gloves on.
2. The gel padding on the knuckles is positioned for proper protection and provides a feeling of confidence and security.
3. There is a stretchy strap just below the knuckles that helps keep the glove in position.
4. The glove fastens around your wrist with an adjustable velcro strap.
5. There is a second strap that fastens over the first one which holds the velcro strap in place and actually provides good wrist support.
6. The gloves are breathable and machine washable.
7. Last but not least, they come in several colors: blue, grey, pink, and red.

CONS
1. Even though I am a bigger guy, I have always worn a large size in every type of glove. Be warned that these gloves run small.
2. While the overall construction is quite good, the sewing around the cut-off fingers is not uniform. The point where the gloves are
cut off (on the inside of the hand) are folded under and stitched together -- at least that was the intention. However the stitching is
"balled up" in different parts and loose strings are evident in some of the fingers. That appears to be a quality control problem.
3. I am assuming that since the gloves are too small for me that the smaller size carries over to make the fingers too tight for comfort.
Perhaps that will loosen up with wear and washing.

So overall I think that this is a great product for what it is intended, but at 65 years old I'm not the guy to punch someone with them on or
to test them out in any manner that would hurt these old bones. At my age I'm trying to protect myself, not break my hands. The manufacturer might want to take a closer look at how the fingers are sewn together, but overall this is a good looking product that should serve its purpose quite well.
text_fidelity_b: Ringside Gel Boxing MMA Hand Wraps

text_fidelity_a:
HYDRONICA Waterproof Backpack Wet/Dry Bag 30L 8 Gallon with Enhanced Shoulder Straps. (Black) Because of the near perfect customer reviews for this bag I gave it a shot. After getting our stuff stolen off the beach in Waikiki a few years ago I never leave anything on the beach anymore. I purchased this bag for an 8 day trip to Maui. For the most part I used it just as a backpack and left it on the beach while someone always stayed back to watch our gear. Kind of sucked that our full group of 5 could not enjoy the water together so on the final 2 days of our trip I took it into the ocean with us. The bag was never completely underwater. I would just let the bag float within an arm's reach near me.

After getting back to the beach and taking my gear out I saw water all over the inside of the bag. Yes, I was careful and folded the top at least 5 times before closing the clasp. I now have two ruined iPhone 6 pluses and a Panasonic point and shoot camera. I'm wondering if I just got a lemon.

This morning I tried the sink test. Dropped some hats into the bag, filled up the kitchen sink, tossed the bag around a bit, and gave the bag a good squeeze. I could see air bubbles immediately. If air bubbles are coming out that means water is getting in. This bag is certainly getting returned. Now I'm wondering who should be responsible for my damaged electronics.
text_fidelity_b: HYDRONICA Waterproof Backpack Wet/Dry Bag 30L 8 Gallon with Enhanced Shoulder Straps. (Black)

Aegend 2 Pack Swim Goggles, Swimming Goggles Anti-Fog for Man Women Youth Adult I bought both round lense and flat lens goggles from this same company with super high reviews.

Everything is a bit blurry with the round lens ones, above and below water. So annoying!

Although I’ve only been pool swimming a few years, I’ve gone scuba diving around the world and worked in the visual arts professionally many years I’m highly sensitized and particular visually.

After reading many swim goggle reviews on amazon, fumbling my way through to find a great pair, thankfully I came across a guy who is an avid swimmer and asserted he never even considers lenses that aren’t flat. It got me thinking… What’s that about?

It’s those funky lenses you see pro swimmers were - for a reason! Everything becomes crystal clear when you put a flat lens goggles on. These are not sunglasses or eyeglasses. Swim goggles are made from very different material that annoy does not uphold clarity when bent. No matter who makes them. (Hence the pros will only wear them..now you’re getting it ;)

I simply couldn’t believe how magically everything became beautifully clear and visible when I put the flat lens goggles on. It’s like wiping grease from a window that becomes a big picture window! All of a sudden you see all the beauty of the sky above, your surroundings, and dancing sunlight under the waterline while you swim!!

(I’m my pic they’re the ones on top)

Whichever brand you buy - BUY FLAT LENS SWIM GOGGLES!!
text_fidelity_b: Aegend 2 Pack Swim Goggles, Swimming Goggles Anti-Fog for Man Women Youth Adult

Sport-Brella Umbrella Chair - 360 Degree Sun Protection Chair I couldn't wait to try this Sport-Brella Umbrella Chair just for the sun protection alone. I thought, what a great idea, sun coverage any where you go outdoors in an instant! The chair is just like any shoulder carry-type folding chair- easy to open, set up and close. It's comfortable on the seating and arms. It has an arm cup holder and front zip pocket for storage with a bottle opener on the zipper tab. The umbrella opens and closes with ease and you can place it on either side of the chair. You can also adjust the umbrella with a full 360 degree rotation.

It's all great except for one major flaw. The umbrella has this teensy tiny plastic tab that you push into either side of the chair that will hold this umbrella in place. The smallest gust of wind lifts the umbrella up and out of the umbrella holder breaking off this teensy tiny tab leaving you with an umbrella that no longer locks in place, and of course chasing an umbrella wherever the wind decides to take it. This was a perfect idea made so cheaply that it makes the best part- the umbrella- pretty much useless in any wind. The gust of wind that lifted this umbrella out of the holder was actually a light breeze, so I can't imagine what a real gust of strong wind would do to this umbrella. It's such a shame that the company SKLZ didn't put in a few cents more for a stronger metal tab which could have made this chair a real winner instead of a waste of a design which is what it really is. It is still a nice chair that does shade you, but only on a very still day when you have no movement of air, which makes the main part I like- the umbrella pretty useless to me.
text_fidelity_b: Sport-Brella Umbrella Chair - 360 Degree Sun Protection Chair

PHILIPS Water GoZero Active BPA-Free Water Bottle with Adventure River/Lake/Spring Water Filter for Hiking, Camping & Fitness Tap Water Filter for Gym, Sport Squeeze Bottle, Lightweight, Blue, 20 oz So it's really cool that we have this because I saw an ad for it one day and thought it was so neat, but that it would probably cost too much. It costs about the same as other water bottles you can get, and then you pay for the filter refills ($17 for a 3 pack and each filter lasts for up to 100 refills!). To me, other than a Brita pitcher, there is nothing else like it out there-- this water bottle is in its own lane.

My son's school requires them to bring a water bottle to school but they don't have filtered water for drinking. This water bottle is GREAT for him so he can have fresh filtered water all day long. It's a SQUEEZE bottle though, so it take a little getting used to-- because you don't want to put your hand on the mouthpiece and then your mouth on it.. and you don't want to pull out the mouthpiece with your teeth constantly (because you'll end up needing braces!). So I tell him to squeeze the water into his mouth without touching the mouthpiece if possible. I drilled little holes into the cap and tied an elastic band through it and the wrist strap to keep from losing the cap-- works like a charm. My kid loves this bottle and says the water tastes good, so it works for me-- drink up! :)

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Instant Screenhouse I have wanted a screen room for ages now as it's impossible to enjoy dinner outdoors after dusk due to the mosquitos and various other bugs. I researched many screened shelters at all price points and decided to give this one a try due to good reviews and affordability.
My friend (male) and I put it up yesterday. Yes, it was easy to put up but not as easy as some other reviewers indicated. Once we got the hang of it, we could see that next time we would get it up in a couple of minutes. As it was, it took about 10 minutes.
Remember that the poles are on the OUTSIDE of the tent. Also, don't extend the poles until you have the screen room in place. Make sure the zippers are open so you don't tear the screen.
OK so the screened room is terrific. It is exactly what I wanted and given the price, I can't believe how happy I am with it. My table and 4 chairs fit nicely into the space. You couldn't really fit more than that in it. We have it on my deck. If I had it on grass or the ground, I would be concerned about bugs coming in through the bottom but as it is, I think it will be ok. My only complaint is that there is not enough weight on the bottom to keep the bottom flaps stationery. I think we may put some 10 lb weights on every side so the flaps don't move in the breeze. I still can't figure out how to keep the zippered flaps open but that's a minor issue. We attached the screened room to the deck so it wouldn't blow away. The instructions say that you shouldn't keep it up for long periods of time because it wil fade in the sun. Since I don't care about that, I'm hoping to keep mine up all summer.
So, in summary - if you are looking for a screened room that does the job and doesn't cost a fortune, buy this. You will be happy with your purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Instant Screenhouse

text_fidelity_a:
Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe I've had my safe for a couple weeks now and I am pretty happy with it. I was looking for an inexpensive safe to keep valuables away from the casual thief. This safe is not going to stop a professional thief. For that type of safe you need to pay upwards of $500. This safe is also not fire or waterproof so if you need those types of features look elsewhere.

The safe weighs about 40 pounds so it is critical to bolt it down, otherwise a thief can just walk off with it. There are 4 holes in the back of the safe and 4 holes in the bottom. There were 4 pretty hefty screws provided, I mounted my safe inside a large cabinet and it seems pretty secure. The safe and door are made of pretty heavy gauge steel so it is not going to be easy to just pry it open.

Inside the safe there are two metal shelves held in place by cheap plastic fasteners. But I will get into that later. Programming the security code was very easy and I had no problem opening and closing the safe. The safe also comes with two keys in case you forget your code or if the batteries die. There is a pretty loud beep when the buttons are pressed but that can be turned off.

I just have two minor issues with the safe. First, the cheap plastic fasteners used to hold the shelves in place are useless. When I opened the safe they were laying in the bottom of the safe with the shelves and half of them were broken. Easily resolved though, I just used metal bolts and screws I had to hold the shelves in place. I think manufacturer should provide these. The second issue I had was with the cheap shelf liners provided. They are very thin foam material and don't stay in place when sliding things in and out. Again though easily resolved by replacing with more substantial liner.

Overall I am pretty happy with this safe. I looked at others in the price range and many seemed to have significant quality issues. The issues I have with this safe are very minor and to be expected for a safe at this price point. This safe is a good value for your money as long as you are just looking to protect valuables from a casual thief
text_fidelity_b: Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe

text_fidelity_a:
MSR Dromedary Bag Water Reservoir With a chronic migraine that hasn’t gone away in years, I’ve slept with a block of ice as the upper half of my pillow for almost as long. It’s just one of the things that really help.

Now, having a container that’ll stay ice cold all night without peeing the bed, that can be a challenge. These are the most durable water bladders I’ve found, and after a year of being frozen and thawed every day, filled to about 85-90% with a little room left for expansion, they show absolutely no real signs of wear. They’ve gotten dirty, and I’ve had to scrub them now and then, but they are very reliable. My only issue has been the tiny nozzle on the little cap, which will occasionally pop open and cause problems. That’s easily fixed with a piece of duct tape. Considering what I put these things through, I really couldn’t imagine finding a better alternative.

It would be nice if they could make the fabric covering a smoother texture, but honestly, that’s a particularly nit-picky detail that most people using these for intended purposes, couldn’t care less about.

These things last so long, if you don’t lose them and you’re not using them in active military service, I seriously doubt you’ll need to replace them for a long time to come. I bet if I’d had one while I was in the army, I’d still be using it. They’re far tougher than the 2-quart canteens I was issued, that’s for sure.
text_fidelity_b: MSR Dromedary Bag Water Reservoir

text_fidelity_a:
Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain First off, these are by far the brightest reflective anything I've ever bought, and I've bought >20 wrist bands, arm bands, leg bands, vests, .... Photons apparently hate this material: every single photon that hits it immediately turns right around and heads back where it came from. You will be seen when you're wearing these. They're so bright you may be seen from space. :)

Second, customer service can't be beat. I ordered both the the wrist bands and the leg bands, but only received the wrist bands. I contacted the vendor, Mark, and he sent the leg bands out within 12 hours of receiving my email. Later I had a problem with the reflective material separating from the neoprene on one one of the wrist bands, and Mark didn't just replace the one that failed, he sent me a whole new pair, and very quickly. So this is a low-risk purchase: if you have any issues, Mark will make it right for you.

One thing I'm not fond of is that the hook portion of the hook and loop closure is too long. Unless the band fits perfectly around your leg, a good sized section of the hook portion will be exposed, and can snag on cyclists' lycra gear. I wish the hook portion was just an inch long. The 3" loop portion would still allow a couple of inches of flexibility re length.

Also, I'm not sure why these have both extra long hook and loop closures and are made of stretchy neoprene. Both seem intended to allow the band to fit different diameters of legs + clothing, so I'm not sure why you need both. And the stretchy neoprene makes it much more likely that the relatively delicate reflective material will separate from it, as happened with 1 of the 4 bands I originally purchased. I'd prefer the fabric to not stretch to minimize the risk of failure, and just use the velcro to adjust the length. But since Mark backs up the product if it fails, this is a small deal.

Overall, I'm happy with these. I believe they're the brightest reflective bands you can buy, so if you want to be seen, these will do the job.
text_fidelity_b: Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain

text_fidelity_a: Lightspeed Outdoors Sun Shelter Tent | Durable Beach Tent Sun Shelter with Clip-Up Privacy Feature | Beach Tent Pop Up with Side-Pull Hub System for Quick Set Up | Fits 3-4 Adults | Hibiscus This is perhaps my husband's only purchase ever that he has made on behalf of our child. I had zero involvement and I was happy to let go of one of "my chores". I approved of the fact that he did his research. Research for me involves countless hours weighing options on the internet, reading reviews, analyzing cost, looking for coupons or discounts, and finally leaving it and a few other finalists to sit in cart limbo for a week or more while I wait for the clear choice to present itself to me in a dream. Research for him involved eyeing a few samples he liked on the beach, talking to the owners about their thoughts, taking a few pictures and then finding the right one online and clicking "add to cart" in One. Single. Day. The tent came quickly. Arrived on time. I picked it up from the post office and was already judgemental and catty about how much the box weighed. Sigh. Why am I like this? Overall the tent is good. We needed something for our 2-year-old son to nap in on the beach so we don't have to pack up and leave at 11:30 everytime. It's time, after all, that we try to reclaim some semblance of our own lives. For this purpose it has worked 3 times. It's too big for our needs but that's not really a complaint and it is a bit heavy but my husband has taken ownership over the whole thing and insists on carrying it himself. He's the only one who has ever assembled or disassembled the thing and he insists it's easy. It seems a bit tall for me to assemble on my own. I wanted it to be the kind that just pops up and folds flat but he liked this one because it had vents. Vents are infinitely more important because it gets hot as a mofo inside when in the direct sunlight and if you can't catch a breeze. I thought the fold up part that stretches to the outside and acts as a sort of patio was stupid at first because who wants to sit or walk on that texture fabric at the beach but it occludes the view of people doing way more fun things than sleeping and for that reason it is essential. It lost a star because of the weight and because one of the loops that secures one of the windows has torn off already and I can foresee it happening again.

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-203 Pedometer with Activity Tracker The Omron is quiet small and light. I can have it in a pocket along with my wallet or iPhone and I don't notice it's there. But I'm skeptical about its accuracy.

I took a few walks and compared the distance it recorded with the route mapped out as a walk in Google Maps. The Omron would typically under measure my distance anywhere from 30 to 60 percent. I re-checked the height, weight and stride settings but that had no effect. I guess it's unrealistic that a pedometer can accurately measure distance.

A more serious flaw is that the unit does not keep lifetime stats -- it's memory is only 7 days. If you have a workout schedule where you need to keep a log of your daily steps, the 7 day memory feature is quite nice for when you forget to write down a day's results, but I would think most people would like to know how many steps they've taken after a year.

While I suppose the distance issue is forgivable -- most people buy a pedometer to keep track of steps, not miles traveled -- the lack of lifetime memory makes it hard to recommend this unit.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-203 Pedometer with Activity Tracker

They are NOT super heavy duty, but they are functional.  They do fit onto a 44mm objective lens.  They could easily be knocked off in the brush, should you have to run thru any.  They do what they are supposed to do, tho.  I shined a flashlight into the unit, and I got no flashback, so I'd say it's good in sunlight.  I also intend to take a small but stout rubber band and put the rubber band over the clamps to help keep the kill flash clamps more snug onto the front of the scope objective lens.  I say again, these will come off if scraped or rubbed very hard against something.  I do believe the best flash killers are the ones that thread directly inside of the objective lenses that have internal threads.  Those options are also a lot more money.  So for the money and function, these flash killers get 5 stars for now.  If they happen to fall off under heavy recoil (I shoot 308 and 30-06), I will change my rating.

text_fidelity_a:
KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym We have a large array of options for working out - to loose/keep off weight and build and maintain muscle. But among the options we wanted something that we could travel with as well as give us a variety of options at home. Boredom can kill a workout routine.

I specifically chose this set for 1. the variety and choices of weights, 2. The options for use with/without a door, 3. The look of the hand and ankle straps and handles, 4. The look of the ends of the bands - their connector including the carabiner connectors.

1. The variety of weights/resistance allows one to go up to 120 lbs. We are not there, but we have the option. Changing the bands out can give a range of weight options and this was a good one compared to others. It also lets one adjust what they are doing - legs, arms.

2. The options for use with or without a door means one can anchor the bands under one’s foot or in a door. We have a TRX set we use with a door, but this gives us another option - we would be more likely to travel with this set now so if unable to use in a door on a trip we would still have the ability to use our feet. That said, there is something “better” to a TRX version. It feels stronger - but it is slightly heavier, while this set is more complicated with all the items included.

3. The hand and ankle straps appeared average overall, but better than some other sets we were looking at. The handles are a bit “rough,” but not uncomfortable. I have worked them with and without gloves and both are fine. The ankle straps are average in feel, but better than some I’ve experienced. Overall both are just fine.

4. I was mostly concerned that they would have longevity. I looked at how the bands connected to the handles, how they were topped off to keep their own ends secure. Compared to others - via pictures - these appeared to have good, solid endings, and that the make up of how they connect to the handles was a good method. I know the carabiners are the weakest link and I took that into consideration. I think they are pretty solid - based on pictures and how they feel - but I am prepared should they fail - we would be able to change them out for others if needed.

Overall we are happy with this choice. The set is what it appears to be, but compared to many others - and I looked at more than 20 sets - this one had everything we wanted, feels as though it has the longevity and strength we wanted and expect, and will give us another successful workout option.

Happy to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym

text_fidelity_a:
PackIt Freezable Utility Cooler, 18 Can, Charcoal Grey The main, cooled compartment is 10.5" x 7.5" x 7" tall. It is a family-sized cooler bag for food or beverages. The gel for cooling is in the front, bottom, and back walls of the cooler. The side walls are just canvas and do not contain gel, and I don't think the top has gel either. The cooler walls can be collapsed so the cooler is flatter and smaller when you place it in the freezer. They recommend cooling it in the freezer for 12 hours before use. There is a zippered, flat outside pocket in the front that is 8.5" wide and 5.5" tall. There is a handle on top of the of the cooler under which is a compartment that will hold things like napkins, phones, utensils, etc. The opening is 5.5" wide. There is no zipper to secure this pocket. Due to the handle being right above the opening for this area, it is not highly convenient to get things in and out. This compartment is about 2" deep and covers the entire width and length of the lid. There is also a zippered, flat outer pocket tucked away on the bottom of the bag. It has an attached pull-out bit of fabric, though I'm not sure what it's for. I'm also not sure what you'd want to place in this pocket, since it's between the ground and the bottom gel wall of the cooler and weight will be on it. The cooler also has an adjustable carry strap. The cooler interior is easy to clean up if there are spills. It seems to be working okay to keep food cool for a few hours while traveling.

This cooler contains polyethylene foam. The advertising says that the "cooler is made from nontoxic poly canvas and has a food-safe, water-resistant lining" and it is made from "...PVC-, BPA-, phthalate-, formaldehyde- and lead-free materials."
text_fidelity_b: PackIt Freezable Utility Cooler, 18 Can, Charcoal Grey

Xantrex 804-1220-02 Batt Chgr, TrueCharge2, 12V 20A, 3 Bank I purchased this charger as part of a system replacing my 15 year old Trace inverter/charger. This a very nice charger- the front panel readout is fantastic- no more guessing what my batteries are doing or what level of charge they are at. I particularly like the equalize feature; my batteries may go through as many as three charge/discharge cycles in a day so it's very important that I am able to equalize them on a regular basis. My only criticism is the size of the terminals for hooking up the battery cables; they are rather small and close together. Standard automotive cables will have too large of a terminal to connect to the posts on this charger without touching each other. The ac input wiring was a little akward too- just a pigtail of three wire with no way to cover the connection without installing a junction box.

Revision: for several months this charger has been intermitantly overheating and not charging my battereies. I thought it was a battery problem since they were reaching the end of their lifespan however I've replaced the batteries and continue to have the same problem. The last time I called Xantrex for warranty issues they were extremely unhelpful but I will give them another chance. Stay tuned for updates.

Dec 29, 2011 I still have not been successful in reaching anyone at Xantrex. First my calls were placed on hold and then after ten minutes I was directed to leave a message. Not one of these messages has been returned.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Sundome Camping Tent, 2/3/4/6 Person Dome Tent with Easy Setup, Included Rainfly and WeatherTec Floor to Block Out Water, 2 Windows and 1 Ground Vent for Air Flow with Charging E-Port Flap I bought this tent in 2017 when I saw it on sale for $39.99 without any intention of using it anytime soon but having one just in case. Due to everything going on this year, I was going nuts being stuck inside so I finally took the plunge and started using it for camping adventures in the Rocky Mountains. So far, so good! I've used this tent 4 separate times now and about 6 nights of sleeping so far. My first trip was a solo one and I had never pitched a tent before by myself. The instructions on the bag tag didn't make the most sense but after about 20 minutes I figured it out on my own. Now I can setup or take down the tent by myself in 5-10 minutes, even less if I have some help.

The included rain-fly is very nice for that purpose as well as providing shade over the mesh openings if you're trying to sleep in a little in the mornings. There are two side windows you can open up for a nice breeze and viewing. Everything zips up nice and easy, however I would advise using both hands when zipping or unzipping the main door. It does have a tendency to catch fabric in the zipper if you're not careful.

I have only slept in the tent by myself so far using a 4" memory foam mattress. Plenty of room for 1-2 people. A family of 3-4 could probably fit comfortably in here with sleeping bags and small children. I don't think 4 adults could sleep too comfortably unless everyone was very cozy with each other.

The included tent stakes are pretty weak. I've already bent almost half of them, so anticipate buying a new set of them at some point. Not a big deal. I had to use rocks to secure my tent better after some high wind gusts blew it around a little bit.

Overall the quality of this tent is very nice and I would buy it again, especially at the price I paid. I see now the price is $69.99 which is probably still a fair price but in that range I would recommend doing some research and seeing if there is a better buy but even at full price this is a good quality tent. So far the coldest I've slept in it was around 40° weather with some light rains and I stayed warm with just a couple blankets, no sleeping bag. I don't know if this would be a good tent for winter camping but I think it would hold up just fine for some late fall snowfall and cold temps when the off-season has begun.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Sundome Camping Tent, 2/3/4/6 Person Dome Tent with Easy Setup, Included Rainfly and WeatherTec Floor to Block Out Water, 2 Windows and 1 Ground Vent for Air Flow with Charging E-Port Flap

12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent Ok, you can decide if I'm either stupid or desperate. One of the biggest problems encountered working in my yard during the summer in Southwest Florida are these insanely aggressive deer flies. They bite hard,even through your shirt, but they seem to particularly like your cheek, neck or lips. They don't stop pestering you until they are either able to feed or you manage to kill them. The best method I have found so far is to patiently wait for one to land on you and then beat the crap out of it. The problem is that I encounter several of them every day.

So I fell for this flypaper on a hat deal, hoping against hope that it would work where other methods have failed. I have used it for four hours every day for five days in a row. The results: NOT ONE DEER FLY CAUGHT! They continue to buzz around me and I continue to impatiently wait for them to settle so that I can kill them, but not even one deer fly even managed to trap itself on the flypaper by accident.

The product headline says "Repellent Strips" but also discloses that it contains no chemicals or odors. If the product has no chemical on it, how does it repel the deer flies? The only way I can see this working is by attaching the strips to a tennis racket and swinging it at the incoming deer flies. At least I'd get some more exercise and maybe kill a few before they can bite me.
text_fidelity_b: 12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent

This allows you to blow it up to your liking. It's comfortable. I have tried folding up clothing to use as a mock pillow and it just gives you a sore neck, so this is a way better option. To put it back in the bag, just open the valve again, press all the air out and roll it up like a toothpaste tube. Then put the band around it and stick it back in the bag. It never goes in quite like it did originally, but it still fits in fine. Then you can use the string on the bag to hang it on a clip on your backpack or purse. The pattern is fun and bright, so you won't lose it anywhere, and the outside is waterproof so it can be wiped off instead of having to put it in the wash like a big pillow. I love having this and my neck will be much happier than when I slept on a balled up sweater.

When I found it listed on Amazon with 240 reviews giving it an average rating of 4.8 stars, I followed my own advice to others and relied on the reviews written here. Normally I use an IWB, Belly Band, or pocket holster for concealed carry, but I also wanted to try an outside the waistband holster for a heavier weapon to see how it felt, how well it concealed (without printing or causing discomfort) and how easily it could be deployed.

So this was a new experience for me as I normally carry smaller and lighter firearms since we live in hot and humid Southwest Florida. I've never accidently displayed any weapon by mistake and have never been called out for "printing". I once even tried an experiment with my wife and had her guess what gun I was carrying and where I had it -- either in my cargo pants or tactical long-sleeved shirt. She guessed that I had a NAA .22 magnum in my right front pocket (Sticky Holster) only because she knew that I had carried one there for over 30 years. What she missed were the three.380's and three 9mm's that I had concealed in two ankle holsters, a Belly Band, another Sticky Holster, and two IWB's (appendix and 6 o'clock).

Now I'm breaking in this Relentless Tatical leather OWB holster which I can use in winter under jackets and in summer under untucked short-sleeved shirts. The holster is extremely well-made, is comfortable to wear, and fits my Defender perfectly. The price is on the money and there's just something about that new leather smell that still gets to me. Not many holsters have 240 reviews written about them. That alone says a lot about how the concealed carry market has recognized and put their stamp of approval on this piece of gear. Give it a fair trial, get used to it, and it it isn't your cup of tea just send it back within the 30 day trial window. I don't think that you'll be disappointed.
